simple.meaning: צוֹא (tsôwʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “soiled (as if excrementitious).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Zechariah 3:3. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the angel.

timeline.evidenceText: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the angel.

He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”

definitions.full: H6674. tso or tsoi [ צֹאִי ] adjective filthy ; — plural צוֺאִים Zech 3:3 , צֹאִים 3:4 (both of garments). צַוָּאר see I. צור .
definitions.rootNote: or צֹא ; from an unused root meaning to issue;
